info.title: Roastwarden API
info.description: A server for coffee roasters: roasts, profiles, profile drive, beans and stock, alarms and notifications. Temperatures are °C, heater and fan are 0–100 %, weights grams. Authenticate with the owner key or an `rr_` token (`Authorization: Bearer …` or `X-API-Key`, Settings → Tokens); reads need no credential unless the server says otherwise (`GET /api/auth/status`). Every error is an `ErrorBody` (docs/control.md, "Errors"). WebSockets: docs/websocket-v2.md.

get.summary: What is running and whether it is well (Settings → About).

post.summary: Restore the MQTT subscriptions, reconnecting when that fails.

get.summary:
Several roasts against one: every number with its difference from the reference, BT,
RoR, heater and fan every 30 s from CHARGE, and from when each roast's BT stays within
`within` °C of the reference's.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The one the others are measured against (default: the first)

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: How close BT counts as together, °C (default 0.5)

400.description: Fewer than 2 roasts or more than 8, or a reference not among them

get.summary: Every approval request, the pending ones first, then newest first. Owner key only.
One approval request by its id (the token that asked waits on it with `?wait=25`).

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
Seconds to wait for a decision (at most 25): the answer comes as soon as the owner
decides, or with the request still pending

post.summary:
Approve a pending request: the held call is made now, as the token that asked; the
answer says what it answered (`result_status`, `result`). Owner key only.
Deny a pending request: nothing is done. Owner key only.

get.summary:
Artisan's machine catalogue (its `.aset` files, embedded): each machine, the Artisan device
it is read through, and whether Roastwarden can set it up from it (and why not).

post.summary:
Plan a roaster from an Artisan machine setup: its connection, register map (roles, each
register's slave), outputs from the sliders and channels from the extra curves, at control
off, with notes on what was guessed or left out. Nothing is saved: `roast roaster add
--artisan` and the dashboard's Add roaster apply the plan through the normal calls.

400.description: Neither or both of machine and aset, or too big

404.description: No such machine in the catalogue

get.summary:
An Artisan setup (`.aset`) that reads this server's Modbus slave: BT, ET, heater and fan
of the roaster it serves, at the slave's port; with the Air and Burner sliders when writes
are on. Load it in Artisan with Help → Load Settings (docs/artisan-screen.md). 404 while
the slave is off (`ROASTWARDEN_MODBUS_ADDR`).

parameters.name: host
parameters.description:
The server's address as Artisan reaches it (name or IP); default: the host this
request was sent to

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Artisan's temperature unit, `C` (default) or `F`: loading the file sets it

400.description: A host that is not a name or an address, or a unit not C or F

get.summary:
Every control command and setting change, with the credential that sent it, newest first
(SECURITY.md, "Audit log").

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Rows with a smaller id than this (paging back).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Only these kinds, comma-separated: control, roast, profile, beans, roaster, settings,
access, backup, other

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Text anywhere in the path, body, token name, signed-in user, roaster, address or
client (case-insensitive for ASCII)

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Only requests sent with the token of this name

parameters.name: failed
parameters.description: Only refused or failed requests (status 400 and up)

post.summary:
Sign this browser in: the owner key or an API token for an `HttpOnly` cookie, `rr_login`,
good for 30 days from its last use (SECURITY.md, "Logins"). Wrong credentials count toward
the 429 like any other. With authentication off it changes nothing.

get.summary: The signed-in browsers (Settings → Logins). The owner's alone.

delete.summary: Sign every browser out, this one too. The owner's alone.
Sign one browser out by its login's id. The owner's alone.

post.summary: Sign this browser out: its login ends and its cookie is removed. Fine to call signed out.

get.summary:
Whether the owner key is on, and what this request's credential is (so the dashboard can
say whether it holds the owner key or a token).
The copies, the last attempt and the next nightly run.

post.summary: Write a copy now; older copies beyond `backup_keep` go once it is in place.

delete.summary: Cancel a staged restore.

post.summary: Check a copy without touching anything: safe at any time.

400.description: Not a copy that can be restored

post.summary: Check a copy and stage it; the next start of the server puts it in place. Owner key only.

400.description: Not a copy that can be restored

get.summary: The green beans, with what is in stock (docs/batches.md).

post.summary: Add a bean; `stock_g` records the first purchase.

Read one coffee from a supplier's product link: a preview, nothing is saved. Save the
draft as a bean (`POST /api/beans` takes its fields), a purchase, or a shopping-list
entry (`POST /api/wanted` with `draft`).

get.summary:
Suggestions for a bean's repeated fields: what was entered before (most used first),
then seeded countries, processes, varieties, certifications and suppliers.
A bean with its stock ledger and roasts.

put.summary: Edit a bean: absent fields are kept, `null` clears the optional ones.

delete.summary: Delete a bean; one that roasts use is archived instead.

get.summary:
A bean's guide (docs/new-bean.md): before its first roast on a roaster, what to expect
(first crack's BT and time on the profile, the supplier quoted); after a roast, while the
bean has fewer than three on its profile, what to change for the next one in seconds or
°C. Only reads: nothing changes a profile or a plan.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: The profile's id (default: the bean's next planned roast's, or the roast `after`'s)

parameters.name: roaster
parameters.description:
The roaster's device id (default: the plan's, the bean's last roast's, else the last
roaster used)

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: For the next roast after this one (a roast of the bean; default its newest)

400.description: `after` is not a roast of this bean

404.description: No such bean, roast or profile

put.summary:
Give a coffee (bean) its own label: the design (`id` or `id@N`), its parameters and a
brand, used for its roasts' labels unless a request says otherwise. All empty clears it.

Edit a purchase or a correction: absent fields are kept, `null` clears. A roast's move
follows its roast.

delete.summary: Take a purchase or a correction out of the ledger.

post.summary: A purchase or a correction: `delta_g` adds (or takes) grams, `set_g` sets the stock.

get.summary:
Whether a roaster is in the middle of something a server restart would cut: a profile
drive, the server's autotune, the cooling after DROP, its heater on, or an open roast with
hot beans. `busy` is true when a real roaster is; the virtual roaster is listed but never
counts. A deploy waits while it is true (docs/DEPLOY.md).
Green coffee month by month: spent, bought, roasted, and what the roasted coffee cost.

post.summary:
A demo visitor's own simulated roaster: made on the first call (with the `rw_visitor`
cookie), the same one after; the shared `virtual_roaster` when the demo is full. Only on a
public demo, and only for a visitor: the owner key and tokens get none.

404.description: Not a demo, or not a visitor (NOT_DEMO)

get.summary: The device profiles (defaults a device starts from).

post.summary: Add a device profile.

get.summary: One device profile.

put.summary: Edit a device profile.

delete.summary: Remove a device profile.

get.summary: The configured devices.

post.summary: Add a device.

Roasters heard on MQTT, with their last status.

post.summary: Try a connection's settings before saving them; the answer says whether it worked.

get.summary: A device with its connections, by registry id or by roaster `device_id`.

put.summary: Edit a device.

delete.summary: Remove a device and its connections.

post.summary:
Add a transport (MQTT, WebSocket, Modbus TCP or RTU, serial TC4) to a device. Its config is
checked for the protocol (a 400 says what is wrong); an enabled connection of an active
device starts polling at once.

400.description: The config does not fit the protocol

put.summary:
Edit a connection: enable or disable it, its priority, its config (checked as when it was
added). Its poller restarts, starts or stops at once.

400.description: The config does not fit the protocol

delete.summary: Remove a connection.

get.summary: A Modbus device's registers.

put.summary:
Replace a Modbus device's registers. The map is checked first (names, kinds, data types,
addresses, word order, scale; a 400 names the register and what is wrong) and the device's
Modbus pollers restart with it at once.

get.summary:
The firmware kinds, the MQTT port a roaster connects to, and the roaster ids whose MQTT
password the server has (`MQTT_DEVICES` and Roasters → MQTT passwords; never the passwords).

post.summary:
An ESP32 sketch with the roaster's id, its MQTT password (from the request, else the
server's: `MQTT_DEVICES` or Roasters → MQTT passwords), the server's address and the Wi-Fi
filled in, as a PlatformIO project in a zip that the Arduino IDE opens too. Nothing is stored. `X-Firmware-Missing` lists what was
left to fill in by hand (`password`, `wifi`).

400.description: A setting that cannot go into the sketch

get.summary: Legacy: the same as `GET /api/replay`.
Whether discovery is on, the broker, the roasters announced and the last publish.
The images and fonts designs can use.
One asset's file.

put.summary:
Add or replace an asset: the request's body is the file (SVG, PNG or JPEG up to 2 MB; a
TTF or OTF font up to 8 MB). A design names it: `image("logo.svg")`, or the font's family.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: with its type's ending: logo.svg, Caveat.ttf

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Where it came from, its licence

delete.summary: Delete an asset (may wait for the owner's approval).

get.summary: The brand kits.
One brand kit.

put.summary:
Add or replace a brand kit: name, tagline, place, website, a logo (an image asset's name),
colours (`#rrggbb`) and fonts. A design reads it as `l.brand`.

delete.summary: Delete a brand kit (may wait for the owner's approval).

get.summary:
Every label design: saved (with their current version and parameters), the owner's
folder, built in.

post.summary: Save a new design (version 1). It must compile: the answer has the check's report.

409.description: The id is taken (saved, built in or in the folder)

422.description: It does not compile: Typst's errors with lines

get.summary:
A design with its source: saved (`sam-gift`, or `sam-gift@2` for a version, with every
version listed), or the owner's folder or a built-in one (`kind`), to start from.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Another version than the current one

put.summary:
Change a saved design: a new source becomes the next version (checked first, as a save
is); name and description change in place.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity

delete.summary:
Delete a saved design and its versions (may wait for the owner's approval). Refused
while a coffee uses it.

post.summary: Go back to an earlier version: its source becomes the next version.

get.summary:
The label printers, the default first, each with its calibrations and what it said when
last asked (nothing is asked now: `GET /api/label-printers/{id}` asks).

post.summary:
Add a label printer: its id, name and address (`ipp://host:631/ipp/print`), and if
wanted its tray, colour, how to send (auto, pdf, pwg, urf) and whether it is the default.

The certificate an `ipps://` printer shows, for the owner to trust (its SHA-256 goes into
the printer's `fingerprint`). Nothing is sent to it.

get.summary:
Look for IPP printers on the network for 4 s (mDNS `_ipp._tcp`, `_ipps._tcp`). It finds
only printers on the server's own network segment: in Docker that needs host networking
(docs/DEPLOY.md); typing the address always works.
One printer, asked now how it is (state, trays, formats); the answer is kept.

put.summary: Change a printer (all its settings, as with add).

delete.summary: Delete a printer and its calibrations (may wait for the owner's approval).

put.summary:
A printer's offset for a sheet: where its labels land. Given as `x_mm`/`y_mm`, or as the
first and last labels' corners from the calibration page (they must agree within 0.5 mm:
more means the printer scales the page or the feed skews, which no offset fixes).

delete.summary: Forget a printer's calibration for a sheet (the sheet's own offset applies again).

post.summary: Make a printer the default: labels go to it unless another is named.

get.summary:
The runs, newest first: what, on which sheet from which label, by whom, and how the
printer's job went.

post.summary:
Make a run: one roast's labels or several roasts' on one sheet (a gift run), each with its
design, settings, brand, copies and QR code, from the sheet's next free label. The PDF is
kept; print it with `POST /api/label-runs/{id}/print`, or download it
(`GET …/pdf`) and mark it printed (`POST …/done`). The same labels as a run made in the
last 24 hours and not yet sent or printed answer that run (200, `reused: true`) unless
`new` is set.

200.description: The same labels as a run not yet printed: that run, `reused: true`

422.description: A design does not compile

post.summary: A run's first sheet as SVG with every label outlined, before making it: nothing is kept.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity

get.summary:
One run: each item (its roast, `design@version`, settings, brand and the data each label
carried) and the printer's job states with their times.

post.summary:
Mark a run printed by hand (its PDF printed from a browser): the sheet's next free label
moves on as when a printer completes a job.

get.summary: A run's PDF, as it was made (print it at "Actual size").

post.summary:
Print a run on the label printer at actual size on label stock. A token's print is always
held for the owner's approval first, with what to load ("a 5163 sheet, labels 1–3
used"); the owner key prints at once. Its job is followed until the printer finishes it.

409.description: No printer is set, or it cannot print now (its state says why)

502.description: The printer refused, aborted the job or could not be reached

post.summary:
A new run with a run's labels as they were (each label's data, `design@version` and
source, settings, brand, QR code), all or some, from another label; print it with
`POST /api/label-runs/{id}/print`.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity

get.summary: Every sheet with its next free label: where a run starts unless told otherwise.

put.summary: Set a sheet's next free label by hand (labels used outside Roastwarden; 1 for a new sheet).

get.summary: What can go into labels: sheets with their offsets, designs, fields, rest days, fonts.

A calibration page for a sheet: marks at the label corners after the saved offset, and
a 100 mm rule. Print on plain paper and hold it over a sheet against the light.

parameters.name: printer
parameters.description: The printer whose calibration for the sheet applies (default the default printer)

post.summary:
Check one label of a design before saving or printing it: Typst's errors with lines, or
a layout report (each line of text with its font, size and box in mm; what runs past
the edge, overlaps, is too small, was shrunk or cut; the QR code's size; which fields
printed) and, when asked, a small PNG. With no roast, sample data.

parameters.name: printer
parameters.description: A printer's id (default the default printer)

post.summary:
Labels from a design's source or a saved design, as a PDF (or the first page as SVG
with `format: svg`): a one-off that is not saved. With no roast, sample data.

422.description: The design does not compile: what Typst said

get.summary:
The roasters that may sign in to the built-in broker: `MQTT_DEVICES`' and those added here,
whether each is connected now and set up under Roasters. Never a password.

post.summary:
A new roaster's password (left out: a random one); it may sign in at once. Answered once:
the firmware download fills it in later, the list never shows it.

400.description: An id or password that cannot be used

409.description: It has one already, it is in MQTT_DEVICES, or the server uses a broker of its own

put.summary:
A roaster's new password (left out: a random one). Connected with the old one, it is signed
out and must come back with the new one; refused while it is busy.

requestBody.description: Optional: a password of your own

409.description: It is busy, its password is in MQTT_DEVICES, or the server uses a broker of its own

delete.summary:
A roaster's password removed: it is signed out and can no longer sign in. Refused while it
is busy. Its roasts and setup stay.

409.description: It is busy, its password is in MQTT_DEVICES, or the server uses a broker of its own

get.summary: What is set up, how each channel's last send went, and the open problems.

post.summary: Send a test through one channel with the form's values, saved or not.

400.description: Not set up, or the channel refused the test

get.summary:
Supplier orders: open ones (ordered or shipped) unless `status` says otherwise, newest
first, with their lines and what is kept of their receipts.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: open (ordered or shipped, the default), all, or one status

post.summary:
A receipt read into an order (`roast order import`): checked (unique per supplier, the
totals to the cent, each line's bean), then recorded as ordered, shipped or received.
Only received writes the purchases. `dry_run` answers the check and writes nothing.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Check only: the totals, the duplicate, each line's bean; nothing is written

409.description: That order or receipt is recorded

get.summary: One order with its lines and receipts.

delete.summary: Remove an order with its lines and receipts; a received order's purchases too.

post.summary: It will not come: cancelled, its shopping-list entries wanted again.

Keep a receipt with its order, as received: the body is the file (an email, web page,
PDF, image or text; at most 5 MB). The same file twice is a 409.

get.summary:
A receipt's file, as received. Private: the owner, or an inventory or admin token.
Always a download, sandboxed: an HTML email never runs in the dashboard's origin.

delete.summary: Remove one receipt from its order.

post.summary:
It came: a purchase per coffee line with its share of the discount, shipping and tax;
a line that arrived different gives its weight (or another bean).
It shipped: the carrier and tracking from the shipping notice.

get.summary: The queue of planned roasts, in order.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: Only this roaster's (and those for any roaster)

parameters.name: done
parameters.description: The roasted ones instead of the queue

post.summary: Plan a roast; it joins the end of the queue.
Put the queue in a new order.

get.summary: One planned roast.

put.summary: Edit a planned roast: absent fields are kept, `null` clears.

delete.summary: Take a roast off the plan.

get.summary: Every profile's share links, newest first (the revoked ones with `all`)

delete.summary:
Revoke a profile's share link: its page and files are then a 404, as for a code that
never was. A profile already imported elsewhere stays there.

get.summary: The profiles, seed profiles included.

post.summary:
Make a profile: BT points, fan, events, curves and the roast level it aims at
(docs/profiles.md).

400.description: Not a valid profile: the reason

post.summary: Import an Artisan `.alog` (or a Roastwarden profile export) as a profile.

400.description: Not a profile it can read

post.summary:
Import a profile from its share link (another server's `https://host/P/CODE`, or one of
this server's): the server reads the shared file (public addresses only, no redirects,
10 s, 2 MB) and makes a profile from it, its description ending with where it came from.
`preview` only reads it.

400.description: Not a shared profile's link, or a profile it cannot make

502.description: The other server could not be read

get.summary: A profile with its points, events and curves.

put.summary: Replace a profile's points; events and curves are kept when absent.

400.description: Not a valid profile: the reason

delete.summary: Delete a profile.

get.summary: Download a profile as JSON that `POST /api/profiles/import/artisan` accepts back.

Download a profile as an Artisan `.alog`, loadable in Artisan as a roast or as a
background profile (docs/profiles.md, "Compatibility notes").

422.description: The profile cannot be written as an Artisan file

get.summary:
The completed roasts of a profile, newest first, with their landmarks: what roast
guidance judges temperatures and times against (docs/roast-guidance.md).
A profile's share links, newest first, the revoked ones too

post.summary:
The profile's share link: its newest one that is not revoked, else a new one (201); `new`
always makes another. The page is public: anyone with the link can see the profile and
import it. It shows the profile as it is now, so later edits show there too.
One order from a supplier: a purchase per bean, the shipping and fees split by weight.

get.summary: The key a browser subscribes with.
The devices that get alarm notifications.

post.summary: Sign a browser up (`PushSubscription.toJSON()` and a name).

delete.summary: Remove a device.

post.summary: Send a test notification to one device, or to all.
A browser turning notifications off names its own endpoint (it does not know its id).

get.summary: Every running drive.
The kinds of report the server makes, and where each is.

A green coffee's report (docs/reports.md, "Coffee report"): what is known of it, stock
and cost, its roasts as a table and small multiples, its cuppings, its ledger.

parameters.description:
`pdf` (the default), `svg` (every page in one SVG: a preview), `png` (one page), or

parameters.name: tz

The offset from UTC in minutes east, for dates and times (default: the `time_zone`

get.summary:
Two roasts compared (docs/reports.md, "Compare two roasts"; docs/analysis.md): BT and
RoR of both on one chart with heater and fan, the phases on one time scale, every number
side by side with B − A, and how closely B's BT followed A's.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
`pdf` (the default), `svg` (every page in one SVG: a preview), `png` (one page), or
`json` (the data the design gets)

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description:
The offset from UTC in minutes east, for dates and times (default: the `time_zone`
setting, else UTC)

parameters.name: roasts
parameters.description:
The roasts by id, comma-separated: A (the one B is measured against), then B. One id:
it is B, against the finished roast before it on its roaster. None: the newest two
finished roasts (on `roaster`), the older as A

parameters.description: With no roast named: only this roaster's

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: How close BT counts as together, °C (default 0.5)

The cupping sheet (docs/reports.md, "Cupping sheet"; docs/cupping.md): a blank form

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
`pdf` (the default), `svg` (every page in one SVG: a preview), `png` (one page), or
`json` (the data the design gets)

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description:
The offset from UTC in minutes east, for dates and times (default: the `time_zone`

The roasts, by id, comma-separated (default: the latest cupping session; none for a

A blank form to score on, with blind codes and the key on its own page (default: the

On a blank form, this many samples of the owner's own as well (default 0; 2 when no

role.description:

`ambient`, `ror`, `heater`, `heater_applied`, `fan`, `drum`, `damper`, `setpoint`,

name, as before.

Mode.description: How a prediction is made, for scoring.

Model.description:
`k·e^{-l·s} / ((1 + t1·s)(1 + t2·s))`. `t2 = 0` is first order with dead time (FOTD).
With `integrating` it is `k·e^{-l·s} / (s·(1 + t2·s))` (ITD when `t2 = 0`): `k` is then the
rate `kv` (output per second per input) and `t1` is unused.

k.description:
Static gain, output per input (°C per %); for an integrating model the rate, output per
second per input.

t1.description: The larger time constant, s (unused when integrating).

t2.description: The smaller time constant, s; 0 for a first-order model.

roaster sends (drum, damper, its channels); null when none since the server started

channels.description: The extra values kept with a roast, drawn and usable in alarms (docs/channels.md)

RobustBox.description:
Ms if the process is not what the model says: the corners Åström & Hägglund and Emerson
use (gain doubled or halved, dead time doubled).

ms.description:

gain_margin.description:
Gain margin (how much the loop gain could grow before it oscillates); infinite when
the phase never reaches -180°.

delay_margin_s.description:
How much more dead time the loop takes before it oscillates, s (phase margin over the
crossover frequency).

crossover_rad_s.description: Gain crossover frequency, rad/s (the loop's speed).

noise_gain.description:
Output change per unit change of the measurement at high frequency (`kp`, plus the D
term's): a sensor step of q moves the output by about this × q.

load_ie.description:
Integrated error after a unit load step at the process input (`1/ki`, output·s per
input unit): smaller rejects disturbances faster.

version.description: The version to go back to: it becomes the next version, so nothing is lost

min_temp.description: BT at which the limit starts to apply.

oneOf.description: The early peak, from the turning point (else 0:15) to 5:00

How RoR fell from first crack to drop, °C/min per minute (least squares; negative
when it falls)

reused.description:

run, so a second Download is the same run (`new: true` makes another)

items.description: Each roast's labels, in the order they go on the sheet (1 to 30)

tz.description:
The offset from UTC in minutes east, for the dates (default: the `time_zone`
setting, else UTC)

printer.description:
The printer it is laid out for (its calibration for the sheet), and printed on unless
another is named then; default the default printer

new.description:
Always a new run. By default a make with the same labels as a run made in the last
24 hours and not yet sent or printed answers that run (`reused: true`), so a second
Download does not keep a second copy

adapt_lookahead.description:
Let the lookahead follow the loop's lag: `lookahead_seconds` is the
most it uses (`docs/replay.md`, "Lookahead").

loop.description: Where the BT loop runs (resolved from device capabilities at start).

A run resumed after a restart cut the last one (`docs/replay.md`, "Resume after a

Auto DROP (`docs/replay.md`, "Auto DROP"): from the profile, off when it has none.

The roaster's fan floor while heating, %: a profile fan below it is raised to it

retail.description: For coffee that is sold: its bag type (the label's data gets the heights it needs)

made (a PDF, not sent), sent, pending, processing, stopped (waiting: paper, a door),

rb.description: Canonical server rate of rise of BT, °C/min.

re.description: Canonical server rate of rise of ET, °C/min.

rd.description: The device's own RoR estimate, if it sent one.

x.description:
Anything else numeric the device reported (ambientTemp, rssi, freeHeap…),
keyed by the original field name.

Samples.description:
A run's record as stored (`GET …/runs/{id}/samples`): time from the start (s), the heater

oneOf.description:
The chosen model's output over the relay part, for plotting against `y` (filled when
served, not stored).

SaveSessionAsProfileRequest.description: `POST /api/sessions/{id}/profile`: save a finished roast as a profile.

The check on sample data (`POST /api/labels/check`): issues do not stop a save,
errors do

Holding power at this fan (the autotune `bias`), % — recorded for
feedforward; not sent yet.

The model the row's gains were designed on (a server run, docs/autotune-2.md): between
two such rows the schedule interpolates the model and designs the gains from it.

tau_c.description: SIMC's knob the row was designed with.

ScreenStatus.description: What `GET /api/about` says of the Modbus slave (null: off).

roaster.description:
The roaster it was told to serve (`ROASTWARDEN_MODBUS_DEVICE_ID`); null: the one real
roaster heard in the last minute

serving.description:
The roaster it serves now; null when there is none to serve (none heard, or more than

last_read_at.description: When a client (Artisan) last read, and its address

charge_enabled.description: At CHARGE: heater power on and the fan to `charge_fan_pct`.

charge_drive.description: At CHARGE: start Profile drive (live) when the roast has a profile.

charge_heater_pct.description:
The heater % the drive's PID starts from. The firmware starts its PID bumplessly from
the output it has, which is 0 with heater power just switched on: that loaded an
integral of about -96 % and held the heater low for the first two minutes. The
sequence sets this in manual first, so the PID takes over from it. 0: no start value.
60 % (about the holding power autotune measured at 100 % fan) tracked the profile
best on the virtual roaster: −13 °C at 0:20 from 0 %, +6.6 °C at 0:40 from 100 %.

drop_enabled.description: At DROP: stop the drive, heater power off, the fan to `cool_fan_pct`.

cool_end_bt_c.description: Fan off and COOL END once BT and ET are below this, °C; 0 leaves the fan running.

cooling.description: The roaster is cooling after DROP (the fan stops at `cool_end_bt_c`)

cooling_roast_id.description: The roast being cooled: its samples are stored until COOL END, Complete or not

extras.description:
What the roaster said about its control with this sample, only the keys it sent
(`heaterApplied`, `rorLimited`, `Kp`, `Ki`, `Kd`, `controlMode`, `heaterEnable`,
`stopCode`, `ff`; migration 037). None before that.

for a roast from before migration 049, the roaster's list now

SetpointTracking.description: BT against the setpoint the roaster was given.

Settle.description: Where BT settles at one heater and fan, by the model.

SetupChange.description:
A change to a setup (the owner's `PUT`). Outputs and floor left out keep theirs, or take the
new kind's defaults when the kind changes.

channels.description: The declared channels (docs/channels.md); left out keeps the saved list.

message.description: A line for the person it is for, on the page ("Happy birthday, Sam"); empty clears it

new.description: A new link even when the roast has one (for someone else, with their own message)

tz.description:
The owner's offset from UTC in minutes east, for the page's dates (default: the
`time_zone` setting, else UTC)

The owner's offset from UTC (minutes east) when it was made: the page's dates (the

Sheet.description:
A stock of label sheets: the page and where each label sits on it (inches). From
gLabels' Avery US templates (docs/labels.md, "Stock").

w.description: One label's width and height (a round label's diameter twice)

left.description: The page's edges to the first label

pitch_x.description: One label's edge to the next one's

SheetNext.description: A sheet and its next free label

next_label.description: The next free label on the part-used sheet (1: a new sheet)

run_id.description: The run that left it so (none: set by hand, or never used)

offset.description: The owner's print offset for this sheet (`label_offsets`)

next_label.description: The next free label on the part-used sheet (1: a new sheet), kept as runs print

ShippedRequest.description: It shipped: the shipping notice's carrier and tracking.

label.description: As the supplier names it: "5 LB"

weight_g.description: Read from the label (kg, lb, oz, g), else the shop's weight

fan.description: Defaults to "the profile has fan data".

adapt_lookahead.description:

loop.description: Where the BT loop runs: `auto` (default), `device` or `server`.

fan_assist.description: Fan assist for this run; defaults to the roaster's saved setting.

Start at this profile time instead of the profile time now (a resume after a
